fix.summary:
Round 5 of #131 is done in /tmp/wt-131. It is still one commit on aab1f210 (3374439f amended into 1fcd4704), with no push and no rebase. Every P1 and blocking item from verify5 and Codex pass 5 was reproduced on 3374439f first, with real uv 0.11.19 and pip 26.2.1, offline. The fix closes the whole class: a source is resolved correctly, then the backend parses the string it is handed a second time.

1. Hand-off. A catalog path now reaches uv and pip as a percent-encoded absolute file:// URI (ResolvedPath.installer_arg, Path.as_uri()). With extras it is 'name[extras] @ file:///...', where the name comes from the wheel or sdist file name or the directory's pyproject [project] name (local_project_name). This applies in build_pip_args and to default verification's staged copy. Measured with 558 real installs: the URI carries [], [x], trailing space, space, ;, %, ?, @, backslash, tab, newline and non-ASCII correctly on both backends. The one exception is '#': uv decodes %23 and cuts there in every spelling, so a resolved path that holds '#' anywhere is now refused. Two consequences: the round-3 refusal of '[...]'-ending names is gone (it installs as named now), and extras on a directory with no readable project name are refused. The Resolved and Install lines still show the path.
2. Scheme case. A known scheme (file, http, https, git, ssh, git+any) written with any capital letter is refused, whether it is the whole source or follows 'name @'. The message says to write it in lowercase. Lowercase URLs pass exactly as written.
3. 'name @ git+...' passes through unchanged. _normalize_git_spec never adds git+ to a direct reference. classify_target routes it as git. The pin identity and source key are read from the URL. 'name @ http(s)://.../r.git' without git+ is refused, and the message suggests the git+ spelling. Measured: uv clones that form and pip fails on it; pip read the old 'git+name @' string as a path in the cwd.
4. Messages. 'file:/abs' is now reported as an unsupported spelling (write file:///...), not as something read from the cwd. The not-fetched message names the offline skip; while AELIX_OFFLINE or PI_OFFLINE is set it says to unset them and refresh online. The no-match note and the failed-refresh message use the same advice. The false 'cache has no copy recorded' for a relative registration now says where the cached copy was read from.
5. Neighbour guard. It runs only for a requirement with no version specifier and compares only its name, so 'local-ext==1.0' next to a file with that exact name goes to the index.
6. New test rows cover: the backslash name, the four terminal-safety values (V02-V05), the None==None guards (V07/V08), V01, V14, V19 and W23. W23 is not equivalent, contrary to round 4's claim; the commit message and ADR now say so. The size-cap wording is corrected, and the ADR Status line and README index row now match.

Docs updated: ADR-0255 (§1, §2 (B)/(C)/refused list/(5)/(9), sweep, §5, §6, a §10 correction, new §11), the ADR-0188 amendment, the guide and its bundled copy, CHANGELOG, and the commit message's REVIEW ROUND 5 section.

owner_decisions: Decision 5 can be read two ways. I implemented it as: the neighbour guard runs only for a requirement with no version specifier and compares only its name. That keeps ADR-0255 (5) true ('a version specifier says package and is not checked'), and 'local-ext==1.0' next to ./local-ext still goes to the index. If the owner meant to compare the name of a versioned requirement too, 'local-ext==1.0' next to ./local-ext would be refused. That is a one-line change, with mutant N24 as the anchor.

Decision 1 assumed '#' would survive a file URI. Measured, it does not: uv 0.11.19 decodes %23 and cuts there. Any resolved path holding '#' is therefore refused for both backends, and the owner may want to accept this narrowing explicitly. Also refused now: extras on a setup.py-only directory, because pip needs 'name[extras] @ uri' and aelix has no name to give it.
follow_ups: Typed path targets ('aelix extension install ./x') and 'extension update' of a recorded path still hand the installer a bare path string. That is the same re-parse class ('#', '[]', a trailing space, ';'), but outside the catalog. Consider the same file:// URI hand-off there.
If TMPDIR contains '#', default verification's staged copy fails installer_arg. The install falls back to the unverified warning (or is refused under --strict).
The Windows hand-off (Path.as_uri() giving file:///C:/...) has not been measured on a Windows host.

blocking.title: Round-6 regression: a typed scp-style git target whose user is not 'git' is now handed raw as a pypi spec, and on uv the cwd repo's build backend runs
blocking.detail: classify_target gained a direct_reference_url branch. direct_reference_url only excludes _SCP_GIT_RE, which matches 'git@' alone, so 'alice@h.example:o/r.git' or 'deploy@git.corp:team/ext.git' parses as PEP 508 'alice @ h.example:o/r.git'. The result is kind=pypi with the raw argv. Base aab1f210 and round 5 3374439f both routed it as git: git+ssh://alice@h.example/o/r.git. With this commit, uv reads the string as 'alice @ file:///<cwd>/h.example:o/r.git', fetches the repository found in the cwd and runs its build backend. That is the #131 cwd-substitution class again, for a typed target, and the consent line says 'Install extension from pypi'. pip fails ('No connection adapters'). 'aelix extension source add deploy@git.corp:team/ext.git' is now refused as 'not a valid source'; round 5 registered '[git] git+ssh://deploy@git.corp/team/ext.git'. No test or doc covers it: ADR (8) still says a typed target keeps its meaning, and the commit message checked only 'scp git@host:path'. Fix: treat [user@]host:path with no '://' and no space around '@' as scp before the direct-reference branch (direct_reference_url and classify_target), and add rows for a non-git user (install argv and source add).

blocking.title: 'aelix extension update' still hands a catalog-installed path to the installer as a bare path string, so the round-5 Codex P1 comes back through update; ADR-0255 section 5 gives an untrue reason for leaving it
blocking.detail: _record_install stores _install_spec(target) = '<abs path><extras>'. 'update' then classifies that string and passes it raw, so the backend parses it again. The case is the same Codex P1 layout: catalog './link' -> 'trusted[]' or 'trusted ', with cat/trusted -> a cwd decoy. discover install puts the right copy in place through the URI. A plain 'aelix extension update --yes' then prints 'Upgrade extension from path: <W>/cat/trusted[]' and installs the decoy. That happens on uv for 'trusted[]' and on both uv and pip for 'trusted '. The commit message and ADR-0255 section 5 list this as a follow-up and say these strings are 'the user's own string, read as the backend reads it'. For a recorded catalog path that is false: the string is the path aelix resolved, which decision 1 says must reach uv and pip as a file:// URI. It is blocking because the measured outcome is the P1 shape this round was meant to close. It was disclosed, though. If the main loop or the owner keeps it as a follow-up, the ADR and commit wording must stop calling it the user's own string.
